subject: HyperVault: intermittent WebSocket stalls during high-throughput inference
messages:
From: Danielle Park <danielle@hypervault.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@hypervault.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Production stalls on websocket during peak load

Hi Priyom,

We hit a production window this morning where our app saw brief (2-10s) pauses in streaming responses for a subset of requests. It looks like the WebSocket connection stays open, tokens stop arriving, then resumes. It's happening during high concurrency (700-900 concurrent streams) and correlates with a throughput spike.

Attached is a screenshot from our client telemetry and a HAR trace from one of the affected flows. Can your team confirm whether this is a client-side backoff or something on Redwood's side (routing/queuing/fallback)? This is impacting a trial cohort; procurement wants to lock terms after the POC but is asking for an incident postmortem before moving forward.

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Head of Integrations — HyperVault
attachments: screenshot-logs-20260210.png, server-trace-20260210.har
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Danielle Park <danielle@hypervault.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Production stalls on websocket during peak load

Thanks for the heads-up, Danielle — sorry you're seeing this. Monica/Marissa: can you triage and confirm whether this maps to the streaming runtime queue/backpressure heuristics or a downstream compute throttling event?

Initial ask:
- Monica — can you pull the serving-side request/response timelines for HV account between 08:30-10:30 ET and share any pattern of long gaps in chunk emission?
- Marissa — can you check if the autoscaler for the customer's dedicated pool (if routed) showed scale events or rejected requests in the same window?
- Dev — please be on standby in case we need a hotfix for chunk flush behavior.

I'll loop procurement if this becomes a contract-risk item. Priyom
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Danielle Park <danielle@hypervault.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Production stalls on websocket during peak load

Quick triage notes (08:30-10:30 ET):
- I see ~42 short stalls (2-12s) across multiple hosts serving the HV tenant. Gaps line up with bursts of new streams creating transient load on the router.
- No request rejections; all requests eventually finish. Latency and token emission pauses co-occur with rapid KV cache misses and a temporary rise in GC on a couple of pods during the spike.
- Stack traces attached for the two pods with highest pause counts.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Increase router worker low-water mark to reduce per-connection batching collapse (short-term config tweak).
2) Collect additional heap profiles during a controlled repro (we might be hitting a memory churn pattern on our runtime threads).
3) Consider an autoscale window smoothing setting for the dedicated pool so scale actions don't coincide with bursts.

Attachments: heap-dump-sample.txt, server-trace-20260211.har

-Monica
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Danielle Park <danielle@hypervault.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Production stalls on websocket during peak load

Follow-up from infra side:
- Dedicated pool (HV isolated routing) showed two instantaneous scale-ups at 08:41 and 09:03 ET. Both completed within the 90s window but aligned with the largest pause windows.
- No node OOMs; ephemeral CPU pressure + increased GC observed on the two serving pods Monica flagged.
- We've staged a config rollback to earlier router batching thresholds and will push at 14:00 ET for a trial repro during customer's daily test.

If the customer sees immediate improvement after 14:00, we can keep the rollback and prepare an incident write-up. If not, Dev/Monica should be ready to enable verbose chunk-path logging for a short window.

-Marissa
Lead Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
